releaseNotes: Made the package standalone and opened the consumer front doors (layering plan phase B; R3, R4, R5, R10, R12). npm pack of skill/formation is now a complete artifact: a files manifest ships bin, core, catalog, knowledge, validation, tooling, starters, the workspace seed, and the entrypoint templates while excluding every development-only surface; tsx and yaml moved to dependencies so a production install actually runs; check:package-parity gained the pack smoke test (npm pack --dry-run, offline) that fails on a missing manifest, a misfiled runtime dependency, an absent layer, or a dev-directory leak — watched failing before first green.

New front doors on the formation bin: setup (formation home + empty registry + health checks + copy-pasteable next steps including the MCP registration line), doctor (read-only health: node, tsx, compiled-catalog/skill-version drift, registry integrity, and the R12 honesty rule — worker CLIs are the machine owner's own subscriptions, so their absence warns rather than errors), new <slug> (a fresh business's birthplace, scaffolded from the audit-proven reference seed with the founder's slug and name stamped in, generated projections excluded, occupied targets refused), list (every registered business with live run-state status), and update (engine update for a git checkout, dry-run by default; anything else is a named error with tag-pinning guidance).

A workspace's catalog pin is now honest about drift (R4): bootstrap names the pinned-vs-engine version gap in every dry-run and re-pins only under --apply, preserving locally modified managed entrypoints; the durable run survives untouched. check:engine-e2e proves the mid-journey re-pin end to end and adds the fresh-business leg — a workspace born from formation new bootstraps, refuses re-scaffolding by name, and plans. Every CLI that takes a path now resolves it against the invoking shell's directory (FORMATION_CALLER_CWD) instead of the package root, so relative --workspace/--dir/--answers/--brief arguments work from anywhere. READMEs document the real journey; nothing listed is unshipped.
